name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-byteen-f1f6

dma_host_support.master_byte_enable: full_word or the device's own size-derived lanes
dma_host_support.reason: the entry feeds the plan's size code and start word into the generated header, the C++ host applies the device's mwb_sel byte enables to the RAM word and refuses a mask the plan does not declare; a mask the device itself does not drive stays refused by name
where: scripts/inprocess_obi_apb_f1f4_spike.cpp (master_select applied with Memory::write, per-byte lane hit counters, guard words)

notes: the same timer/target, DMA profile and four-word block as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-f1f6.json; only the declared transfer size differs, so the destination byte enables are the device's own

dma_transfer_size_bytes 1 makes the plan derive ZipDMA size code 3 in both size fields: the start word becomes 0x00330000 (bits 17:16 and 21:20), and one four-word block is 16 one-byte source beats and 16 one-byte destination beats

the host pre-fills the four destination words and one guard word on either side with 0xa5a5a5a5, so the case line shows the assembled words (dst0..dst3), the per-byte lane coverage (dma_lane_written 16, dma_lane_missing 0, dma_lane_extra 0), that nothing outside the block was strobed (dma_bytes_outside_block 0) and that both guard words are unchanged

the source reads are full-word reads: the host answers each read with the RAM word and the device's own realigner shifts the byte it asked for, which is why the case records dma_read_lane_partial rather than a full-word read count
